skill.name: conflict-resolver
skill.description: Analyze Git merge conflicts and guide safe manual or assisted resolution.
skill.summary: Guides developers through Git merge conflict analysis, resolution choices, and post-merge validation.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown fences, conflict markers, or illustrative application code and were marked false positive. Specific command guidance was confirmed where it can mutate repositories, change global Git settings, or execute package scripts. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Repository-mutating Git commands are presented as direct examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running checkout, rm, clean, rebase, add, commit, merge continuation, or pull commands.

remediation.issue: The auto-resolution script can stage files after choosing ours or theirs with simple heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Make the script dry-run by default, show each diff, and require per-file approval before checkout or staging.

remediation.issue: Validation steps run project-controlled npm scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that npm scripts can execute arbitrary local code, especially in untrusted repositories, and require confirmation.

remediation.issue: Global Git configuration commands persist across repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer repository-local configuration examples or clearly label global configuration as a persistent user choice.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Conflict Resolution Can Discard Work
semantic_findings.description: The suggested auto-resolution script checks out ours or theirs and stages files using whitespace heuristics. This can silently discard one side of a conflict if an agent runs it without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly uses git checkout --ours/--theirs and git add inside an automated loop over conflicted files.

semantic_findings.title: Project Script Execution During Validation
semantic_findings.description: The checklist and verification script recommend npm lint, test, and build commands. In untrusted repositories, package scripts can execute arbitrary local code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly invoke npm run lint, npm test, and npm run build as validation steps.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Global Git Configuration Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends global Git configuration changes for merge behavior and tools. These changes persist beyond one repository and can surprise later workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited sections use git config --global for merge settings, rerere, and merge tool preferences.

content.value_statement: Merge conflicts slow delivery and create risk when developers choose changes without context. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code analyze conflicts, compare intent, and plan safe resolutions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies content, structural, semantic, and formatting conflict types.
Explains ours, theirs, manual, and three-way merge strategies.
Shows merge conflict examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, and package files.
Provides Git command references for status checks, staging, merge tools, and configuration.
Suggests post-resolution checks for markers, linting, tests, and builds.
limitations: It is guidance, not a verified merge engine.
Automatic scripts need human review before they change files.
It cannot prove business logic is correct without project tests.
It may not cover repository-specific merge policies.

use_cases.title: Resolve feature branch conflicts
use_cases.description: Compare both sides of a conflicted file and choose a combined resolution when both branches add useful behavior.

use_cases.title: Review risky merge decisions
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed resolution discards behavior, hides validation, or needs follow-up tests before merge completion.

use_cases.title: Teach Git conflict workflows
use_cases.description: Explain conflict markers, common Git commands, and verification steps in a simple order for learners.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Conflict
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one conflicted file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the conflict markers in this file and list the safest manual steps to resolve them.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate decision between ours, theirs, or combined changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare both sides of this conflict and recommend ours, theirs, or a combined resolution with reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-File Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced merge with related conflicts across files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related conflicts across files, identify shared intent, and propose an ordered resolution plan.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Resolution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before continuing a merge or rebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the proposed merge resolution for semantic regressions, missing tests, and follow-up checks before commit.

output_examples.input: A React import conflict where both branches add different imports.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies both needed imports, preserves the correct hook path, and recommends linting the file.

output_examples.input: A package file conflict where one branch changes the version and another adds a script.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends keeping the newer version, retaining both script entries, and running package checks after review.

output_examples.input: A rebase with repeated conflicts in moved and modified files.
output_examples.output: The skill groups the conflicts, suggests resolving one file at a time, and recommends recording repeated safe choices.

best_practices: Review the intent of both branches before choosing a side.
Run read-only inspection commands before mutating the working tree.
Confirm tests and code review after complex resolutions.
anti_patterns: Do not accept all current or incoming changes without reading context.
Do not run auto-resolution scripts on valuable work without a dry run.
Do not ignore remaining conflict markers after staging files.

faq.question: Does this skill resolve conflicts automatically?
faq.answer: It provides strategies and example scripts, but users should review changes before any command modifies files.

faq.question: Can it handle semantic conflicts?
faq.answer: It helps reason about intent and API changes, but project tests and human review remain necessary.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The network-looking examples are application code snippets inside merge conflict examples.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the included commands?
faq.answer: Some commands modify files, Git history, or global Git settings. Confirm each command before execution.

faq.question: What should I do after resolving conflicts?
faq.answer: Check for remaining markers, run suitable tests, build affected areas, and request review for complex merges.
